about: The numbers every engine's tests of the external-event budget are held to
(ARCHITECTURE.md, "External-Event Budget"), for the document
`tests/integration/external_chain_is_bounded.scxml`.
Why a shared table: seven tests (the C++ interpreter and its AOT twin, and
the Rust, Go, Kotlin, Python and C11 AOT drivers) each wrote the default and
the four budgets below as their own literals. A budget moved in one engine
and its test changed with it, and nothing compared the engines. The numbers
are the contract; each test reads them from here, drives its own engine with
them, and asserts the outcome this file states. A test asks the engine for
its limit nowhere: an engine's own answer agrees with any limit, including
one an edit moved by three orders of magnitude.
Each outcome is one machine, entered from `idle` and never left (the
document's header says which chain each event starts). A number is a
counter the document's own `<assign>`s keep, read after the calls named.
spin        no budget is set: the call takes `default_budget` events and
leaves the rest queued, so `links` is `default_budget - 1`
(the host's event is the first of the call) and one chain
was truncated
exact       `bounded` is the host's event and five `lap`s, six in all, so
a budget of 6 refuses nothing
one_short   a budget of 5 leaves one `lap` queued and says so
resume      a budget of 20 takes the host's event and nineteen beats; the
next call (a `poke`) takes the rest, each in a budget of its
own, to thirty beats, and hears the `poke`
static_zero `delay="0ms"`: whether an engine queues it straight to the
external queue or hands it to its scheduler differs per engine,
so only the budget is shared and each test keeps what it holds
zero_expr   `delayexpr="'0ms'"` through the scheduler: entering the state
pops nothing; one tick pops `budget` entries at one reading
and says it left the due one waiting
timed       eight pulses, each due a millisecond after the last, are not
a runaway however small the budget: nothing is truncated
host        a host chooses the budget, and a budget that takes no event
is refused without changing the one in force
across_sessions
a different document, the C++ Interpreter's own: a parent and the
child it invoked ping each other, each with a loop and a budget of
its own. The parent's budget cuts the chain: the host's `go` and
`budget - 1` rounds, and one chain was truncated. `rounds` is a
property of that document, stated here beside its budget
budget_between_calls
a budget a host sets between two calls governs the next one: a
budget of 3 takes the host's event and two beats of the `resume`
chain and cuts it; a budget of 100 then takes the whole remainder
in one call, to the thirty beats and the one truncation `resume`
states, and that call is not cut
